A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MixGRPO. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the original methods, tables and qualitative examples can be matched across versions despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation experiments, training-overhead measurements, ablations and cross-dataset evaluations in Tables 1–14 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v6 retains those empirical results and adds a CPS sampling comparison and text-to-video training experiments in Table 15 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: v6 adds MixGRPO-CPS, replacing the original stochastic SDE update with Coefficients-Preserving Sampling in an additional variant (Section 12, Equation 25). The original GRPO objective, sliding-window scheduler and MixGRPO-Flash algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates text-to-image generation using HPDv2 and Pick-a-Pic. v6 retains this coverage and adds text-to-video alignment with HunyuanVideo-1.5 and prompts from DanceGRPO, substantially extending the task to temporal generation and motion quality.

E2.justification: Table 15 and Figure 10 introduce a direct comparison between CPS and standard SDE sampling within MixGRPO, with FLUX also shown. Existing DanceGRPO, Flow-GRPO and offline/online Flow-DPO comparisons are retained; the new video experiment reuses Flow-GRPO.

E3.justification: The added video experiment introduces a distinct protocol: eight 121-frame videos per prompt at 480×864, HPSv3 and VideoAlign rewards, Muon optimization, and window settings w=6 and tau=100. A separate CPS comparison uses three reward models and 300 training steps. These are new experimental designs; existing image protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v6 adds a controlled SDE-versus-CPS sampler study with quantitative and qualitative evidence, plus analysis of video training-reward dynamics. The existing window, solver, hybrid-inference and cross-dataset ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new video reward trajectories do not define a statistical uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Tables 1–14 retain their values. New Table 15 reports SDE versus CPS scores of 0.2344 versus 0.2382 for Pick Score, 1.5901 versus 1.6449 for ImageReward, and 0.3648 versus 0.3692 for HPS-v2.1. New video curves favor MixGRPO particularly on HPSv3 and visual quality, and Figure 10 adds CPS examples. These are additional results, not revisions of the original four-reward comparison.

T1.justification: Section 12 adds explicit SDE and CPS transition equations, including the new CPS update definition and its coefficient-preservation claim. The original convergence proof and DPM-Solver++ derivation in Sections 7–9 are unchanged; no additional CPS proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about mixed sampling, sliding-window optimization and acceleration, including the approximately 50% and 71% training-time reductions. The supplemental extensions do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v6 newly links SDE-induced grainy artifacts to reward hacking and argues that CPS provides cleaner reward feedback. It also attributes improved video training to a reduced optimization search space. The existing reward-model limitations and earlier mechanism discussions remain.

D1.justification: v6 documents settings for the added CPS and video experiments, including fixed initial noise, 64 H800 GPUs, Muon learning rate and weight decay, video dimensions, batch construction and reward weighting. Existing implementation details and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds references for CPS, Muon, HPSv3 and HunyuanVideo-1.5, and positions CPS as a more principled sampling alternative. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against earlier GRPO methods are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged. v6 adds brief CPS references in the main text, new supplementary Sections 12 and 12.1, and author/affiliation edits; the visualization section becomes Section 13. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v6 adds Table 15, the four-panel video reward plot in Figure 6, and CPS examples in Figure 10. Figure 1 moves to page 2, Tables 11–14 are packed more tightly, and the original supplementary Figures 6–8 become Figures 7–9 with their examples retained.

improvement.justification: The controlled CPS comparison and documented video experiment make the sampler choice and applicability beyond images better supported while retaining the original evidence. The gain is limited: video evidence consists of training-reward curves without reported uncertainty, and the claim of consistent monotonic improvement overstates Figure 6. These additions strengthen the paper modestly rather than resolving a major deficiency.
